audit.method: Manual semantic grading. Each criterion is one bit; a bit passes only when every stated conjunct is explicit. No partial credit and no inference of omitted owners, limits, dates, caveats, actions, or semantic roles.

criterion_order: C1 primary problem, chosen decision-rights intervention, and explicit deferrals/rejections
C2 observations/claims/unknowns, required classifications, and causal rival
C5 complete closure and four required result branches

bits.rationale: It makes decision latency/ambiguity primary and rejects the COO and council, but it rejects broad or informal delegation, not broad reorganization; that required disposition is not explicit.
It does not explicitly separate observations, stakeholder claims, and unknowns, nor explicitly place boundary quality and future effects among the unknowns.
It names the Head as routine decision owner but not one end-to-end implementation/go-live outcome owner; it also lacks a named absence backup and names only a generic customer-facing owner.
The six-week test has scope, records, measures, and safeguards, but no named evidence owner and no explicit dated intermediate checkpoint.
The closure lacks the required add-capacity result and does not name a next owner/action for every result branch.
It correctly targets decision latency/ambiguity and defers the COO and approval council/new layer, but never explicitly rejects or defers a broad reorganization.
The memo discusses evidence and caveats but does not explicitly classify the required observations, stakeholder statements as claims, and all required unknown types.
The Head owns routine exceptions, not an explicitly end-to-end implementation/go-live outcome; customer continuity is split, so the required single outcome-owner role is absent.
Although reversible and measured, the trial never names an evidence owner for the tracker/dashboard.
It offers only three qualitative outcomes, not the four required measurable branches, and omits branch-specific next owners/actions.
It selects decision rights and rejects the COO/council, but does not explicitly reject or defer broad reorganization.
No explicit observations/claims/unknowns separation is provided, and the required stakeholder statements and unknown categories are not all classified.
It assigns decision and communication responsibilities but does not name one accountable end-to-end go-live outcome owner.
The pilot is bounded and measured, but no role explicitly owns the evidence record/dashboard.
The closure has continuation, narrowing, and expansion language but lacks the required four complete branches, exact one-variable revision, full-cost capacity gate, and next owners for each.
It makes the queue the primary problem and rejects the COO/council and undifferentiated broad delegation, but does not explicitly reject or defer broad reorganization.
It has a caveat section but no explicit observations/claims/unknowns ledger and does not classify stakeholder statements as claims.
The Head owns delegated decisions and their record, not the end-to-end implementation/go-live outcome, and no actual absence backup is designated.

The reversible May 4-June 12 pilot names the CEO/Head as change owners and the Head as record owner, uses derivable intermediate reviews, defines scope and January-March baseline, preserves a register, measures outcome/harm, and includes continuity, promise, specialist-review, suspension, and traceability safeguards.
The closure omits the required add-capacity branch and branch-specific owner/action assignments.
It selects bounded decision rights and rejects the COO/council, but explicitly rejects broad delegation rather than broad reorganization.
It never explicitly separates observations, claims, and unknowns or classifies all required stakeholder claims and unknown types.
The Head is the accountable decision maker and Customer Success owns communication, but no one role is explicitly accountable for the end-to-end implementation/go-live outcome.

The May 5-June 15 reversible trial names change owners and Implementation as log-evidence owner, has derivable installation and weekly checkpoints, uses the January-March baseline and specified artifacts/measures, and covers continuity, unauthorized promises, specialist review, temporary narrowing, and retained evidence.
The mixed-result branch does not require exactly one revision once; the capacity branch lacks a benefit-above-full-role-cost threshold; and every branch does not name its next owner/action.

It explicitly identifies the decision queue/interface as primary, selects bounded decision rights, rejects the council, defers the COO/capacity layer for lack of evidence, keeps the organization flat, and restores the prior model by domain rather than by broad reorganization.

The observed/claimed/unknown ledger and causal rival are explicit, but it does not explicitly identify the quality of the proposed exception boundary or the pilot's future effects as unknown; those semantic roles cannot be inferred from a generic 'full mix and quality' caveat.

The Head owns end-to-end implementation decisions and one go-live date; the design provides domains and observable limits, specialist consultation, notice, clocks and escalation destinations, interface expectations, absence coverage, a decision register, Head-owned continuity, and retained security/contract review.

The reversible May 5-June 15 pilot names change/evidence owners, May 18 and June 1 checkpoints, scope, baseline/artifacts, measurable outcomes/harms, and explicit continuity, promise, qualified-review, rollback, and evidence-preservation safeguards.
The capacity switch does not require the residual gap's value or relief to exceed the full role cost, so the required add-capacity result is incomplete.
It identifies the correct primary mechanism and rejects the COO, council, and another layer, but does not explicitly dispose of broad reorganization as a separate option.

It explicitly separates observed facts, stakeholder claims, and unknowns; treats tracker/shadow/utilization/runway as state or observations; makes live sustainability, boundary safety, causal attribution, and future residual effects uncertain; and names multiple causal rivals.

The Head owns on-time supportable go-lives and continuity, with complete decision domains/limits, consultation, notification, escalation destinations and clocks, interface service levels, CEO/absence backup, decision log, customer communication ownership, and qualified security/contract review.

The six-week reversible test names owners and evidence roles, May 6 start, May 18/June 1 checkpoints and June 15 close, affected scope, baseline/log, outcome and harm measures, plus all required safeguards and record-preserving rollback.

The revision branch says to name an owner later instead of naming the next owner now; keep and capacity actions also rely on global ownership rather than naming each branch's next owner, so the every-result owner/action conjunct fails.
The memo correctly targets centralized routine approval and ambiguity and rejects the COO/council, but never explicitly rejects or defers broad reorganization.

The ledger expressly separates observations, claims, and unknowns; includes the required source categories; treats accepted-pattern completeness, sustainable live workload, hidden future effects, and causal attribution as uncertain; and states a capacity/judgment rival.

It gives the Head the correct on-time outcome, defines domains/limits and specialist review, supplies same-day notice and escalation clocks/destinations, sets interface service expectations, names CEO and implementation backup coverage, requires an auditable log, assigns continuity communication, and retains security/contract protection.

The dated six-week reversible test has named change/evidence owners, May 6/7 installation, May 18 and June 1 reviews, June 15 close, explicit scope/baseline/artifacts/measures, and every required safeguard including pause and record preservation.
The add-capacity branch never requires benefit to exceed full role cost, and the revise branch defers naming its owner instead of naming one; therefore the four-result closure is incomplete.

It clearly selects the right intervention and rejects the COO/council plus headcount, title, committee, and compensation changes, but broad reorganization itself is not explicitly rejected or deferred; a reporting-line or responsibility reorganization is not excluded by that list.

It explicitly classifies observations, stakeholder claims, and unknowns; treats tracker/shadow/utilization/reported runway as evidence/state, and live outcomes, sustainable load, prior-pattern correctness, causal attribution, and future benefit/cost as uncertain; it also names a capacity/complexity rival.

The Head owns each implementation through go-live and the design explicitly covers domains and limits, Customer Success consultation/notice, destination and escalation clocks, interface expectations, owner and CEO backups, a complete audit register, continuity ownership, and unchanged qualified security/contract review.

The May 5-June 15/16 reversible pilot names change and evidence owners, May 25 review, scope, January-March baseline, register, direct outcome/harm measures, and explicit safeguards for continuity, promises, qualified review, rollback, and evidence preservation.

The memo states the current decision and unknowns, preserves domain-specific CEO preapproval, and supplies measurable Keep, one-variable/one-time Revise, full-cost-gated Add-capacity, and harm-triggered Rollback results. The header and branch text name the CEO/Head/qualified reviewers as next owners and give each an action.
It makes the recurring queue and ambiguous authority primary, chooses decision rights, and rejects the COO/council, but does not explicitly reject or defer broad reorganization.

It separates observations, claims, and unknowns; includes tracker, shadow, utilization and reported runway as evidence/state; marks sustainable load, customer effects, boundary quality, missing-record cause, and future needs unknown; and names hidden complexity/rework as a rival.

The Head owns the end-to-end implementation outcome, and the design includes routine domains/limits, consultation/review, notice, escalation triggers/destinations/deadlines, service expectations, owner backups, the decision log, Customer Success continuity communication, and security/contract review.

The six-week reversible test has named change/evidence owners, May 4-8 installation, May 25 interim and June 15 final review, scope, baseline/log, observable outcome/harm measures, and safeguards for continuity, unauthorized promises, specialist review, rollback, and evidence retention.

The add-capacity branch requires decision latency to meet target but does not explicitly require interface causes to be addressed, and the keep/revise/capacity branches do not each name their next owner; both omissions fail the all-conjunct closure.

findings: The frozen generation and response integrity checks reproduced without a blocker.
Control earned only the pilot-design bit in reps 4 and 5; its dominant failures were missing explicit evidence taxonomy, missing end-to-end outcome ownership, and incomplete four-branch closure.
All guided responses passed the complete operating-design and pilot-design criteria.
Only guided rep 1 explicitly disposed of broad reorganization; the other guided responses rejected narrower structural changes but did not state that semantic role.
Only guided rep 4 completed the strict four-result closure, including full-cost capacity gating and branch ownership/action.
The normalized guided-minus-control effect is +0.56, exceeding the predeclared +0.20 gate by +0.36.
